subject: Re: Log sanitization engineering handoff — trace IDs & header masking

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: log retention and redaction gaps — next steps

Hi Sam / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the immediate engineering handoff so we can get a baseline implementation on your side for review: 

1) Scope we agreed: request/response logs stored for 30 days in your VPC deployment; we need to redact PII and any authorization headers.
2) Specific items you flagged:
   - Trace IDs in X-Trace-Id header "should not be linkable to tenant IDs" (Alex's wording)
   - Certain headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email) must be removed or masked before write to long-term logs
   - Sample logs: you asked for a sanitized example showing best-practice masking rules

Action items: 
- Ben (engineering): propose a short implementation that masks trace IDs and strips the listed headers; include a fallback that retains a truncated, hashed trace token for internal correlation. Please draft an internal spec (<=1 page) by EOD Friday.
- Jasmine: I'll share the redaction spec draft and the sample logs we discussed.
- Sam/Alex: review Ben's spec and confirm whether keeping a hashed-trace token (SHA-256 prefix) is acceptable for correlation with your internal observability.

Attachments: redaction_spec_draft.pdf (draft we discussed), example-logs.txt (sanitized sample).

Thanks — feel free to ping if anything above is off.

—
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Re: Post-call: log retention and redaction gaps — next steps

Thanks Jasmine — quick clarification from our security team:

- We can accept a hashed trace token, but only if the hash is one-way and salted per-tenant. We cannot have trace IDs that allow cross-tenant correlation (that's the main ask).
- For headers, Authorization and Cookie must be removed entirely; X-User-Email must be redacted.
- We also asked about masking for response bodies where PII might appear in free-text fields — can Redwood provide a confidence score for automated redaction so we can gate retention?

Can Ben include the proposed salt approach and the redaction confidence output in the spec? If you can send an update by EOD Friday ET, we'll route it to our security folks.

Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Security | Finova Payments
sam.torres@finova.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: log retention and redaction gaps — next steps

Hi all —

Following up with the implementation outline Sam asked for. High level plan (draft):

1) Header handling (ingest path):
   - Strip Authorization, Cookie at the API edge.
   - For X-Trace-Id: replace value with H = first 12 chars of HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, tenant_salt). Store H as x-redwood-trace-token. Original trace_id is never persisted beyond in-memory request context.

2) Body PII detection and masking (sync pass):
   - Run a lightweight PII classifier on request/response bodies. For detected spans, store masked text (e.g., ******* or tokenized placeholder) and emit a redaction_confidence float [0.0-1.0] in the log entry metadata.
   - Confidence threshold default = 0.85 to retain; items below threshold get redacted and flagged for manual review (tag: needs_review).

3) Retention and access controls:
   - Logs persisted to encrypted S3 within customer VPC for 30 days; access limited to customer IAM + Redwood audit role for support cases (time-limited access, recorded in audit log).

4) Telemetry for audits:
   - Emit an immutable audit record for any feature that unsanitized data is accessed; include who, why, and a short reason field.

Open questions I will address in the final spec:
- Salt management: propose KMS-backed per-tenant salt rotated quarterly; need Finova sign-off on rotation cadence.
- Performance: latency impact is minimal for short payloads; we'll include benchmarks in the next update.

Attached: short markdown snippet with examples (pasted below). Planning to push a one-page spec to the shared drive by EOD Friday PT.

Example (sanitized):
Original header: X-Trace-Id: 7f34b2a1-...
Stored header: x-redwood-trace-token: d3af4b9c1e2a

Let me know if this meets your requirements or if we should include tenant-salt rotation in the initial rollout.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: log retention and redaction gaps — next steps

Sam —

Thanks for the quick review. Ben's approach looks aligned with what you described. Two quick clarifications from our side before we finalize: 

- We'll implement per-tenant salts via your KMS integration. Ben's team will include KMS key policy suggestions in the spec.
- For redaction confidence, our default retention gating will be 0.85 — items below that will be redacted and surfaced to a manual queue. We can tune after initial rollout.

Next steps / timeline: 
- Ben to upload the 1-page implementation spec + micro-benchmarks to the shared drive (link below) by EOD PT today.
- If Finova approves, we'll schedule a 30-minute eng sync next week to walk through the sample logs and the salt rotation plan.

Jasmine
